Hi Jonas / Ben,

Thanks for the time last week. VertexOps is moving quickly on an AWS listing and we want to coordinate the 'sell-with' eligibility items and connector certification steps so the listing launch supports co-sell motions with your field. High-level asks from our side:

- Confirm the technical evidence we need to provide for AWS listing (sample telemetry, integration diagram, test account).
- Alignment on pricing commitments and any SKUs Redwood expects for co-sell eligibility.
- Timeline for a go/no-go gating decision from Redwood (we're targeting an AWS marketplace publish by mid-August).

I've attached our internal checklist and a short PDF of the AWS listing requirements we use. Can we set a short working session with your partner ops + tech enablement folks tomorrow? 30 minutes should be enough.

Attachments:
- VertexOps_SellWith_Checklist.xlsx (xlsx)
- aws_listing_requirements_v2.pdf (pdf)

Jordan —

Appreciate the deck and checklist. We can run a focused sync tomorrow at 11:00 PT. For prep, a couple of quick items from our side:

1) Technical evidence: we need a deployed integration in an isolated test account plus a short test plan that demonstrates end-to-end telemetry and auth flows. A sample events log (scrubbed PII) is helpful.

2) Listing SKUs & pricing: Redwood's co-sell playbook requires a minimum of two SKUs that map to usage tiers (developer / production) and a clear overage policy. We'll share a template pricing grid.

3) Security/compliance: If you have SOC2 or ISO artifacts, please share a pointer. If not, we'll need a short risk worksheet for the listing committee.

I'll add Vivek for the marketplace entitlements conversation.

See you tomorrow — joining details to follow.

—Jonas

Quick follow-up after reviewing the checklist and the sample artifacts VertexOps uploaded. Two notes that will determine co-sell path: 

1) SKU shape: For AWS co-sell eligibility, we generally require one committed-tier SKU (monthly commit) OR a clearly advertised enterprise plan with minimum contract language. On-demand-only SKUs typically don't meet our co-sell threshold unless there's an explicit field rebate structure.

2) Billing integration: If you plan to route billing via AWS Marketplace (Metering Service), confirm whether VertexOps will accept Marketplace percentage fees — we can model economics but need confirmation for contract language.

Action items for VertexOps:
- Provide proposed SKU matrix (names, list price, billing type: committed vs on-demand) by COB Monday 7/16.
- Confirm SOC2 pointer or provide completed risk worksheet (see template in Drive).

I'll start drafting the entitlements checklist and will post a HubSpot task (HS-482911-VTX) to track approvals. If Procurement needs to loop in legal or signature flow, share DocuSign contact; we typically route final listing agreements through DocuSign.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
